before_conditions: A limit order is being appended to an existing price level that already contains at least one earlier order.
The newly appended order is written to storage with its prevOrderId field left as 0.
The prevOrderId link update is applied only to an in-memory copy of the order, not to the stored order.
The price level's linked list contains earlier orders that precede the appended order.
required_property: When an order is appended to an existing price level, its prevOrderId must be persisted in storage so that the doubly-linked list remains intact, ensuring that later removal of that order does not detach or orphan the earlier orders at that price and that makers retain access to their collateral.
bad_outcome: When the appended order is later cancelled, fully filled, or expires, the removal routine treats it as the head because prevOrderId is 0, rewires the head to the next order, and drops the earlier orders from the list; those ghost orders become unreachable for matching, amending, or cancelling, permanently locking makers' collateral, inflating open-interest accounting, and consuming limited tree nodes.
